title: Generally spherical object with floppy filaments to promote sure capture
abstract: An amusement device featuring a substantially spherical configuration formed from numerous floppy, elastomeric filaments radiating densely from a central core region. The filaments collapse upon impact to absorb energy and prevent bouncing. Their plurality and floppiness enable them to quickly thread between fingers during catching, while their high-friction surfaces promote secure grip.
gist: The Koosh ball: thousands of thin rubber filaments joined at a core to form a sphere that doesn't bounce, collapses on impact, and threads between fingers so it is almost impossible to drop — designed so children who fear hard balls can always make the catch.
